Reference / archive/tar

archive/tar#

Complete uncompressed TAR writing: default PAX, or explicitly strict USTAR.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let archive = TarArchive(entries); // binds traversal, no encoding yet
let bytes = archive.bytes();       // complete independent in-memory value
let output = TarWriting(sink);     // borrowed Writing, no output yet
output.write(member); output.finish(); output.close();

Description#

Complete uncompressed TAR writing: default PAX, or explicitly strict USTAR. All seven entry kinds are values; no extraction or filesystem/account lookup. Default absent mode is 0755 for directories, 0644 otherwise; absent ownership is 0/0 with empty names. Explicit values, including zero, are preserved. UTC calendar metadata converts exactly to epoch seconds/nanoseconds.

PAX retains UTF-8/long names, large IDs, negative/fractional times and comments using local length-framed records. Strict USTAR rejects unrepresentable values rather than truncating. Device numbers fit seven octal digits in both formats. Every written header has an unsigned checksum; padding and two EOF blocks are zero. GNU and base-256 are never written; ParsedTar can read both.

object TarWriting#

object TarWriting does WritingArchive, Closing

Resource owner: only private path-tracking and lifecycle buffers. The sink is borrowed. finish writes two zero blocks and flushes once; close/destroy never finalize or flush. Processing Errors propagate unchanged and poison the writer; no retries, rollback or implicit completion. finished() performs no I/O. After close only close/closed remain valid. Names are retained for exact duplicate checks (linear lookup); payloads are not retained between calls.

object ParsedTar#

object ParsedTar

Bounded immutable TAR input projection, with no I/O or resources. entries() reparses the bound bytes and yields a self-contained indexed snapshot. It accepts USTAR/GNU headers, local/global PAX and GNU long-name/long-link records; sparse formats and V7 are rejected. Every header checksum, numeric field, payload/padding span, effective path/link and duplicate is checked. Two zero EOF blocks are required; extra complete zero blocks are accepted. Padding is strictly zero. Local extensions must have a following real member.

ArchiveLimits is spent BEFORE copying file bytes. Separate cumulative extension budgets default to 1 MiB and 4096 headers; the four-argument overload sets both. Failure reports tar_metadata/tar_extensions via ArchiveLimitExceeded. The caller already owns origin: these are NOT bounds on its original allocation. Names decode strict UTF-8; sub-nanosecond time is rejected unless extra digits are zero. Returned metadata contains explicit mode/ownership, including zero.

let entries = ParsedTar(bytes, ArchiveLimits(20,1024,8192,255)).entries();
entries.first().path().string(); // immutable; no stream or file retained

object TarReading#

object TarReading does ReadingArchive, Closing

Consuming TAR resource over a borrowed Reading. Constructors perform no input reads. entry() returns one independent member after validating its padding, without reading the next header. finished() is passive; normal EndOfArchive is remembered only after two zero blocks, optional zero blocks and source EOF. A framing layer must bound Reading to this archive if further data follows.

Limits match ParsedTar, including the optional metadata bytes/header limits (defaults 1 MiB/4096). Headers are 512 bytes; other read requests are <=8192 and never exceed an admitted span. Positive short reads are normal. Empty reads inside a span or oversized source returns are InvalidTar. Admission, duplicate and path checks happen before payload I/O; every header checksum is checked.

Source Errors preserve identity and poison the resource, even EndOfArchive thrown by Reading itself. Format/limit/path Errors do the same. No retries. close/destroy release only private state, never read/drain/close the source. After failure/close only close/closed work; close is idempotent. No cursor. Previously returned entries are not cached and survive resource closure.

let archive = TarReading(source, ArchiveLimits(20,1024,8192,255));
let entry = archive.entry(); // may throw EndOfArchive
archive.close();             // caller still owns source
